title: Marzahn Berlin - FAQ
subtitle: How the estate was built, what to see, and how to plan a day out.

items.a: Site works for the large estate began on **3 March 1975**. The first new block was topped out on **2 September 1977**, and Marzahn became its own Berlin district on **5 January 1979**.

items.q: How many flats are in Marzahn?
items.a: The district office counts about **100,000 flats** in the large estate of Marzahn-Hellersdorf, where two thirds of the district's residents live.
Yes, for a day. Combine **Alt-Marzahn** with its village church and windmill, the **Gärten der Welt** and the free **Wolkenhain** platform on the Kienberg, then take the U5 back.

items.q: How do I get to Marzahn from the city centre?
items.a: Take the **S7** to S Marzahn, about 20 minutes from Alexanderplatz, or the **U5** to U Kienberg (Gärten der Welt) for the gardens and the hill. A normal **AB ticket** covers both.

items.q: How much are the Gardens of the World in winter?
items.a: From **1 November to 28 February** adults pay **EUR 4**. The gardens open daily from 9:00 until dusk; some gardens and the cable car take a winter break.

items.q: Can I visit the Marzahn windmill?
items.a: Inside visits are only on the **first Sunday of the month from April to October**, 11:00 to 16:00. In winter you can see it from outside on the walk through Alt-Marzahn.
A furnished GDR flat at **Hellersdorfer Straße 179**, near U Cottbusser Platz. berlin.de lists it as open on **Sundays 14:00 to 16:00** with free entry; check before you go.
